claim: MiCS minimizes communication scale (the number of participants in a collective) rather than communication volume, so collectives stay inside the fastest available group.
stance_target: the claim that on a 5-GPU box the right sharding scope is all five cards in one flat group, since there is no faster tier to retreat to
scope_conditions: Cloud clusters with heterogeneous, hierarchical networking
quoted_support: In this paper, we propose MiCS, which Minimizes the Communication Scale to bring down communication overhead. Specifically, by decreasing the number of participants in a communication collective, MiCS can utilize heterogeneous network bandwidth, reduce network traffic over slower links, reduce the latency of communications

claim: DGX-class clusters have intra-node bandwidth only about 3x faster than inter-node, whereas public-cloud V100 instances on 100 Gbps networks have intra-node bandwidth about 24x faster than inter-node.
stance_target: the claim that the bandwidth hierarchy ratio, not absolute bandwidth, determines which sharding strategy is appropriate
scope_conditions: DGX-2/DGX-A100 with InfiniBand vs cloud V100 instances with 100 Gbps networking
quoted_support: These nodes are connected via high-bandwidth low-latency InfiniBand leading to clusters whose intra- and inter-node GPU-to-GPU bandwidth is nearly balanced (intra-node bandwidth is about 3x faster than inter-node). ... cloud instances with V100 GPUs are typically paired with 100Gbps networks, in which case the bandwidth is less balanced (intra-node bandwidth is about 24x faster than inter-node).

claim: ZeRO's flat all-device partitioning is ill-suited to clusters where intra-node bandwidth far exceeds inter-node, because it ignores the network hierarchy.
stance_target: the claim that FSDP/ZeRO defaults assume a balanced fabric, which a PCIe-only box definitely is not
scope_conditions: Public-cloud clusters with unbalanced intra/inter-node bandwidth
quoted_support: By treating these devices equivalently and not accounting for the heterogeneous and hierarchical nature of the inter-node network, ZeRO fails to take advantage of the faster intra-node networks.

claim: MiCS achieves 2.89x throughput over DeepSpeed on V100 clusters with 100 Gbps networks, and up to 2.74x on A100-40GB clusters with 400 Gbps networks.
stance_target: the size of the win available from scale-aware partitioning on commodity networks
scope_conditions: AWS V100 100 Gbps and A100-40GB 400 Gbps clusters
quoted_support: On V100 GPU clusters with 100Gbps network, the system throughput of MiCS is 2.89x larger than that of DeepSpeed ... On A100 GPU clusters with 40GB memory per GPU and 400Gbps networks, MiCS is up to 2.74x as fast as DeepSpeed.

claim: MiCS reaches 99.4% weak-scaling efficiency and trains a 100B-parameter model at over 170 TFLOPS per A100 across 512 GPUs.
stance_target: the achievable scaling efficiency when communication scale is controlled
quoted_support: MiCS gets near-linear (e.g., 99.4%) weak scaling efficiency in the cloud ... MiCS has been deployed to train a proprietary model with 100 billion (B) parameters, saturating over 170 TeraFLOP/s (TFLOPS) per A100 GPU with activation checkpointing at the scale of 512 GPUs.

claim: MiCS beats Megatron-LM-3D by up to 30.1% throughput on commodity cloud networks.
stance_target: the claim that 3D parallelism (TP+PP+DP) is not automatically the best topology when the fabric is weak
quoted_support: Compared to Megatron-LM-3D, a state-of-the-art system specialized for training Transformer models, MiCS achieves up to 30.1% better throughput.

claim: MiCS combines scale-aware model partitioning with a hierarchical communication strategy to reduce the scale of each collective.
stance_target: the concrete mechanisms available for adapting data parallelism to a hierarchical fabric
quoted_support: Scale-aware model partitioning. Instead of using all devices as a ... Hierarchical communication strategy. Hierarchical communication ... reduce the scale of each collective communication.

claim: ZeRO's communication overhead grows larger as cluster size grows, because effective bandwidth falls with collective scale.
stance_target: the claim that a small 5-GPU world size avoids the scale-driven latency penalty entirely
scope_conditions: ZeRO on clusters up to 512 GPUs
quoted_support: And the communication overhead of ZeRO grows larger as the size of the cluster scales up
